papers.title: Altermagnetic signatures and topological textures in ultrathin multiferroic BiFeO3
papers.authors: Geo Fratian, Maya Ramesh, Xinyan Li, Evangelos Golias, Yousra Nahas, Sebastian Maria Ulrich Schultheis, Julian Skolaut, Marti Checa, Arundhati Ghosal, Evan Krysko, Paul Malinowski, Brendan D. Faeth, Jan Priessnitz, F. C. Fobasso Mbognou, Atsushi Hariki, Kosuke Sakurai, Mizuki Furo, Shashank Kumar Ojha, Morgan Congdon, Shiyu Zhou, Alexander Qualls, Kai Litzius, Christoph Klewe, Peter Meisenheimer, Jan Kuneš, Kyle Shen, Laurent Bellaiche, Libor Šmejkal, Darrell G. Schlom, Yimo Han, Sergei Prokhorenko, Ramamoorthy Ramesh, Paul Stevenson, Angela Wittmann, Lucas Caretta
papers.abstract: Magnetoelectric multiferroics promise low-power switching, non-volatile memory and signal transduction, yet practical deployment requires ultrathin films in which polar and magnetic order often degrade. Uncompensated bound charge drives depolarization in ferroelectrics, whereas off-stoichiometry, reduced anisotropy and charge transfer can produce magnetic dead layers. Here we realize a multiferroic phase of BiFeO3 with no dead layer, revealing signatures of emergent altermagnetism in the ultrathin limit. First-principles calculations, symmetry analysis, atomic-resolution imaging and magnetic imaging show that short-circuit electrostatic boundary conditions and epitaxial strain drive a continuous, thickness-induced phase transition accompanied by multiferroic topological textures. At four unit cells, these boundary conditions stabilize a collinear monoclinic phase with d-wave altermagnetic order, supported by magnetic circular dichroism and spin-resolved photoemission measurements. These results establish a pathway to stabilize unconventional multiferroicity at device-relevant thicknesses, reframing scaling limits for oxide electronics. Epitaxial strain and a metallic SrRuO3 bottom electrode are used to stablilize a monoclinic phase in four-unit-cell BiFeO3 thin films. A broad suite of measurements are used to support the presence of both ferroelectricity and d-wave altermagnetism in these ultrathin films.
papers.summary_en: The authors report ultrathin BiFeO3 films with no magnetic dead layer and signatures of d-wave altermagnetism in a four-unit-cell monoclinic phase. Their results link epitaxial strain and electrostatic boundary conditions to a thickness-induced multiferroic phase transition and topological textures.

papers.title: Nonlinear responses induced by inhomogeneous edge states in a centrosymmetric topological insulator
papers.authors: Yitian Guo, Chengxin Jiang, Chenxi Liu, Zhanbo Fang, Yanjun Li, Jingyan Song, Dong Qiu, Kewen Zhang, Huazhan Liu, Hao Hong, Yichao Yan, Shengyuan A. Yang, Yuqiao Zhou, Yang Wang, Jie Xiong, Chao Yang, Jianjun Ying, Hui Zhang, Haomin Wang, Xixiang Zhang, Yan Li, Peng Li
papers.abstract: Nonlinear electrical responses, second-order transport effects beyond Ohm’s law, typically arise in systems where inversion symmetry (P) or time-reversal symmetry (T) is broken, such as in non-centrosymmetric crystals exhibiting the nonlinear Hall effect, or in magnetic systems showing non-reciprocal transport. Here, we report the unexpected discovery of nonlinear electrical responses, under T symmetric conditions, in a bulk centrosymmetric, non-magnetic topological insulator, ZrTe5. We show that this nonlinearity is modulated by external magnetic fields, measured position and the Fermi level (EF) shifting, originating from the evolution of inversion symmetry breaking induced by inhomogeneous spatial distributions of surface edge states (ESs). Our findings unveil a mechanism for nonlinear transport in centrosymmetric systems and highlight an additional route for designing nonlinear electronic responses based on topological surface states. Second-order electrical nonlinearity is conventionally thought to originate in crystals with noncentrosymmetric lattices or magnetic order. Here, the authors show another generation paradigm in bulk centrosymmetric, nonmagnetic ZrTe5, arising from an inhomogeneous surface edge-state distribution.

papers.title: Time-reversal-symmetry-breaking spin injection from a compensated magnet
papers.authors: Jone Mencos, Antonin Badura, Eoin Dolan, Sebastian Beckert, Rafael González-Hernández, Nicolás Sigales, Tim Kokkeler, Ismaïla Kounta, Matthieu Petit, Charles Guillemard, Anna Birk Hellenes, Warlley Campos, Javier Rial, Dominik Kriegner, Vincent Baltz, Luis E. Hueso, Jairo Sinova, F. Sebastian Bergeret, Olena Gomonay, Tomáš Jungwirth, Libor Šmejkal, Lisa Michez, Helena Reichlova, Fèlix Casanova
papers.abstract: The generation and transport of spin currents are central to spintronics, a technologically relevant field in which information is carried and manipulated using the electron spin rather than solely the electrical charge. Conventionally, electrical spin injection and the separation of charge and spin currents rely either on ferromagnets1–10, in which spin polarization originates from a net magnetization, or on relativistic effects such as the spin Hall effect11–16. Here we demonstrate spin injection from Mn5Si3, a compensated magnet with vanishing net magnetization. Using lateral spin-valve devices, we electrically inject spins from Mn5Si3 into a non-magnetic channel and detect their propagation at a spatially separated ferromagnetic electrode. Switching between time-reversed magnetic states of Mn5Si3 reverses the detected spin signal, demonstrating that the spin injection breaks time-reversal symmetry. This behaviour is observed for two distinct electrical-biasing geometries, providing a characteristic signature that differs from conventional ferromagnetic and spin-Hall injection. Symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations and spin-transport modelling show that our observations are consistent with the altermagnetic order of Mn5Si3, in which spin-polarized currents can arise despite the absence of net magnetization17–21. The calculations yield spin polarizations of 6.5–10%, comparable to those of conventional ferromagnets, whereas the spin-transport modelling of the experiments indicates spin diffusion lengths of 50–130 nm. Our results provide experimental evidence that a compensated magnet can generate spin currents controlled by its magnetic order and demonstrate that the altermagnetic properties of Mn5Si3 enable spintronic functionality without net magnetization. Experiments show that altermagnetic Mn5Si3 generates spin currents despite zero net magnetization, demonstrating a central prediction of altermagnetic spintronics.
papers.summary_en: This study demonstrates electrical spin injection from compensated, zero-net-magnetization Mn5Si3 into a non-magnetic channel, with the detected signal reversing when the magnet switches between time-reversed states. The results are consistent with altermagnetic spin polarization and establish a route to spintronic functionality controlled by magnetic order without net magnetization.

papers.title: Narrow carbon pentaheptite nanoribbon as a covalent metal
papers.authors: Jianmin Huang, Qitang Fan, Jie Meng, Jia Liu, Jie Cui, Jianing Wang, Yi Li, Ruoting Yin, Honghe Ding, Junfa Zhu, Mengchun Ye, Shijing Tan, Chuanxu Ma, Yao Zhang, Qunxiang Li, Jinlong Yang, J. G. Hou, Bing Wang
papers.abstract: Metallic carbon-based nanoribbons are sought after1,2 as atomically defined one-dimensional conductors with potential relevance to future carbon-based electrodes and interconnects3, ideally with quantum-limited conductance comparable to metallic carbon nanotubes4. Metallic graphene nanoribbons have been realized by band engineering, notably through zero-mode superlattices1. However, atomically precise metallic nanoribbons of fully non-benzenoid carbon allotropes, such as the theorized metallic carbon pentaheptites5,6, remain unexplored. The realization of these nanoribbons could enable bottom-up fabrication of all-carbon electronics7,8 compatible with semiconducting graphene nanoribbons9–13 and nanographenes14,15, along with their fascinating properties16–20. Here we report a hierarchical approach for the on-surface synthesis of planar carbon pentaheptite nanoribbons (CPHNs) by laterally fusing well-aligned polypentalene chains transformed from pre-synthesized polycyclooctadiene chains. Two distinct types of narrow pentaheptite nanoribbon share a similar basal structure consisting of a central heptagon chain flanked by either identically (CPHN 1) or differently (CPHN 2) oriented polypentalene chains on opposite lateral edges. CPHN 1 is an intrinsic metal, whereas CPHN 2 is a narrow-bandgap semiconductor. The CPHN 1 ribbon exhibits near-ballistic conductance approaching one conductance quantum, comparable to metallic carbon nanotubes4. This highlights CPHN 1 as a promising planar carbon metal and suggests a possible route towards carbon quantum wires, although further synthetic optimization will be required for device integration. Planar carbon pentaheptite nanoribbons are synthesized by laterally fusing polypentalene chains transformed from pre-synthesized polycyclooctadiene chains, suggesting a possible route towards carbon quantum wires.

papers.title: Subcycle videography of Landau–Zener–Majorana transitions in graphene
papers.authors: V. Eggers, G. Inzani, M. Meierhofer, L. Münster, J. Helml, R. Wallauer, S. Zajusch, S. Ito, L. Machtl, H. Yin, C. Kumpf, F. C. Bocquet, C. Bao, J. Güdde, F. S. Tautz, R. Huber, U. Höfer
papers.abstract: Abstract Strong light fields have unlocked entirely new possibilities to tailor coherent electron trajectories, engineer band structures and shape emergent phases of matter all-optically 1–9 . Unravelling the underlying quantum mechanisms requires a visualization of the lightwave-driven electron motion 10,11 directly in the band structure. Although photoelectron momentum microscopy has imaged photoexcited electrons averaged over many cycles of light 12–19 , subcycle band-structure videography has been limited to small electron momenta 8,20 . Yet, lightwave-driven elementary processes in quantum materials often occur throughout momentum space. Here we introduce attosecond-precision, subcycle band-structure videography covering the entire first Brillouin zone and visualize one of the most fundamental but elusive strong-field processes: non-adiabatic Landau–Zener–Majorana tunnelling. The interplay of strong-field-driven acceleration within the Dirac-like band structure of graphene and periodic Landau–Zener–Majorana interband tunnelling manifests in a coherent subcycle displacement and distortion of the carrier distribution at the Brillouin zone edge. The extremely non-thermal electron distributions also allow us to disentangle competing scattering processes and assess their impact on coherent electronic control. Our panoramic view of field-driven electron motion enables a new quality of microscopic understanding of strong-field control of quantum materials.

papers.title: Electric Field-Induced Hole- and Electron-Type Flat Bands in Twisted Double Bilayer Graphene

At 3.1°, gate-induced doping can produce flat bands between the valence-band maximum of the bottom bilayer and the conduction-band minimum of the top bilayer.

papers.abstract: Application of a finite electric field and small twist angle between two graphene bilayers leads to widely tunable electronic structures that support emergent phenomena. Here, we measure the electronic structure of twisted double bilayer graphene with twist angles of 3.1$^{\circ}$ and 6.0$^{\circ}$ using micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (microARPES) on \textit{in situ} gated samples. At a twist angle of 6.0$^{\circ}$, we find that the dispersion around the valence and conduction band extrema is unchanged compared to separate graphene bilayers, whereas electric field tunable hybridisation gaps and band flattening effects occur at higher binding energies. In the 3.1$^{\circ}$ structure, we find that the resulting superlattice drives dispersion changes around the valence and conduction band edges. Increasing the gate-induced doping in the bottom bilayer leads to the formation of flat bands between the valence band maximum in the bottom bilayer and conduction band minimum in the top bilayer. Our experiments establish combinations of twist angle and electric field that potentially support strong electron-hole excitations and that provide a benchmark for the theoretical description of moderately twisted double bilayer graphene.

papers.abstract: Strange metals pair a resistivity linear in temperature with a specific heat $C/T$ rising logarithmically on cooling. papers.abstract: Frustration in magnetic systems gives rise to unconventional orders and exotic spin liquids. Here, we explore a new type of frustration arising from an intrinsic bond-dependent orbital-field that couples orbital degrees of freedom to spin correlations. Introducing this orbital-field interaction into the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model on the honeycomb lattice, we show that local spin-orbital constraints generate a subextensive degeneracy, lifted by order-by-disorder to select distinct collinear magnets in a cascade of phases as the orbital field increases from a para-orbital liquid. At larger fields, the selected phase gives way to an incommensurate unidirectional spiral that spontaneously breaks chiral symmetry. This transition is driven by the coupling of a Goldstone mode to gapped dynamical spin-orbital fluctuations. The spin stiffness becomes negative along a particular direction, while the spiral wavevector grows as the square root of the distance from the transition, signaling a Lifshitz-type transition. We present a microscopic route to realizing this orbital field and discuss candidate materials.

papers.relevance_reason: This is an original theory of frustrated quantum magnetism that predicts a field-driven sequence of magnetic phases and a Lifshitz-type transition.

papers.abstract: The formation of topological flat bands near the Fermi level in kagome-structured metals has generated substantial research interest. One key consequence of this electronic structure is the strong anisotropy in charge transport, such as the significantly higher in-plane resistivity relative to the out-of-plane direction. However, the spin transport properties of these flat-band kagome metals are still largely unexplored. In this work, we investigate spin-charge conversion in CoSn, a representative flat-band kagome metal. Scanning tunneling microscopy is employed to image the CoSn surface with atomic resolution, and $dI/dV$ spectroscopy shows clear signatures of the flat bands. Using magneto-optical techniques, we quantify the spin-orbit torque (SOT) in bilayers of ferromagnetic nickel (Ni) and c-plane CoSn thin films. We find a large effective spin Hall angle of $θ_{SH} = 0.484 \pm 0.005$ within the CoSn layers, significantly exceeding the value measured for Pt of $θ_{SH} = 0.0436 \pm 0.0003$ in Ni/Pt bilayers. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations provide a microscopic understanding of the intrinsic spin Hall effect in CoSn, elucidating the sources of Berry curvature in momentum space. These findings establish kagome metals as promising materials for efficient spin-charge conversion and low-power spintronics.

papers.abstract: In non-centrosymmetric bulk materials, electrons flowing in the opposite directions often exhibit different properties. This diode-like effect (i.e., non-reciprocal electron transport) typically originates from relativistic spin-orbit coupling, and its amplitude scales with external magnetic field or magnetization in ferromagnets. Although such rectification is usually absent in antiferromagnets at zero field, recent theories predict that non-coplanar antiferromagnetic order can host large non-reciprocity even without spin-orbit coupling, magnetization or external magnetic fields. This phenomenon - the spontaneous topological diode effect - can potentially be used for efficient electrical readout of antiferromagnetic domains, while it has not been verified for real materials. Here, we report the observation of this effect in a chiral-lattice non-coplanar antiferromagnet CoTa3S6. Nonlinear resistivity measurements reveal the non reciprocal nature of electron transport along the [001] direction at zero field. The observed non-reciprocity exceeds that in typical ferromagnets, whose amplitude is governed by antiferromagnetic order parameter rather than magnetization. First-principles calculations show that the non-coplanar antiferromagnetic order induces asymmetric band dispersions even without spin-orbit coupling, establishing the non-relativistic origin of the observed response. The present findings demonstrate a new mechanism for efficient electrical readout of antiferromagnetic domains, and highlight non-coplanar antiferromagnets as a promising material platform for realizing ferromagnet-like functional responses without relying on spin-orbit coupling or magnetization.

papers.abstract: We show that a class of pyrochlore materials provides a route to realize 3D Quantum Hall insulators, based on magnetic texture and flat band interference. We study itinerant electrons on a pyrochlore lattice Kondo-coupled to localized moments living on another interpenetrating pyrochlore lattice, with the moments forming a field-selected three-in/one-out texture. The noncoplanar texture generates complex spin-dependent hopping amplitudes and unequal local exchange energies, reconstructing the compact-localized parent flat bands into narrow bands separated by a global three-dimensional gap. The low-energy states are concentrated predominantly on kagome planes within the three-dimensional lattice, reflecting the combined effects of quantum interference and the texture-induced sublattice potential. When the lowest band is fully occupied, the response is characterized by a Chern triplet $\mathbf{C}=(1,1,1)$ and reciprocal Hall vector $\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{H}}=(2π/a)(1,1,1)$, giving $σ_{yz}=σ_{zx}=σ_{xy}=e^2/(ha)$. The quantized bulk Hall response enforces chiral surface spectral flow, visible as noncontractible Fermi loops at the surface. Our work opens a new direction in the search for three-dimensional quantum Hall physics in magnetic pyrochlore systems, and suggests a broad design principle based on the interplay of magnetic texture and flat-band interference.

papers.abstract: A transition between an integer quantum Hall insulator and a chiral spin liquid can become critical without closing the single-electron gap, raising the question of which composite excitations govern the change in topological order. We investigate this question in the \(\mathrm{SU}(3)\) triangular-lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard model at one particle per site and magnetic flux \(π/3\) per triangle. Using infinite density matrix renormalization group calculations, we identify a weak-coupling integer quantum Hall phase and an interaction-driven \(\mathrm{SU}(3)_1\) chiral spin liquid. Near the transition, both the neutral and charge-\(3e\) correlation lengths increase substantially, whereas the single-electron correlation length remains short, providing evidence for a Chern--Simons--Higgs critical theory, where a gauge-invariant monopole carries the quantum numbers of a fermionic \(\mathrm{SU}(3)\)-singlet trion. We discuss the implications for doping the system and recent experiments on doping \(ν=-2/3\) fractional quantum anomalous Hall in tMoTe\(_2\).

papers.abstract: Conventional altermagnetic spin splitting arises from staggered exchange and sublattice-dependent anisotropic hopping without requiring spin-orbit coupling (SOC). Here we derive a low-energy effective model showing that SOC and staggered exchange can jointly activate additional spin splitting on momentum planes where the nonrelativistic contribution vanishes. In hexagonal $α$-MnTe, this SOC-activated contribution produces d-wave spin splitting near $Γ$ with out-of-plane spin polarization. Its leading angular pattern counter-rotates by half the in-plane Néel-vector rotation angle. First-principles spin-transport calculations reveal a corresponding approximate half-angle locking between the Néel-vector orientation and the electric-field directions maximizing the signed longitudinal and transverse spin conductivities. Analytical transport calculations based on the effective model trace this locking to the same angular coupling between momentum and the Néel vector that governs the spin-splitting pattern. Our findings connect the microscopic mechanism of SOC-activated altermagnetic spin splitting to directional spin transport, providing a theoretical basis for probing Néel-vector orientation and controlling spin-current generation.

papers.abstract: Exciton-phonon coupling (ExPC) governs energy relaxation and exciton dynamics in photoexcited quantum materials. Recent advances have revealed rich and tunable excitonic phenomena in moiré superlattices, yet the microscopic mechanisms underlying the coupling between moiré excitons and moiré phonons remain elusive. Here, we develop a real-space representation for moiré ExPC based on a unified theoretical framework combining the many-body Bethe-Salpeter equation with phonon perturbation theory. Furthermore, we uncover a general real-space selection rule: the spatial matching of a moiré exciton's electron and hole densities with the moiré-phonon-induced potential perturbations determines their individual coupling contributions, while coherent interference between the electron and hole contributions controls the total ExPC. We demonstrate this rule in prototypical WSe2/WS2 moiré heterobilayers, revealing pronounced exciton- and phonon-mode-dependent coupling, including nearly complete suppression of ExPC through destructive electron-hole interference. These findings establish the internal electron-hole spatial configuration of moiré excitons as a key degree of freedom governing the strength and mode selectivity of their coupling to moiré phonons, opening opportunities to engineer ExPC through spatially tailored moiré potentials.

papers.abstract: The superconducting diode effect (SDE) is characterized by unequal critical current magnitudes for opposite-polarity current flow, owing to broken spatial-inversion and time-reversal symmetries. For a superconducting pair wavefunction to spontaneously break inversion symmetry implies the formation of Cooper pairs with nonzero momentum, yielding a nonuniform superconducting state. For singlet superconductors, the formation of such a (FFLO) state has long been understood to provide an escape from high field Pauli pair-breaking -- how and why such an effect might occur for equal spin pairing is an open question. Here we report the observation of a large SDE in bulk specimens of the three-dimensional heavy-fermion triplet superconductor UTe$_2$, with a peak diode efficiency of 33% at the high magnetic field strength of 33.6 T, representing the highest-field observation of the SDE to date. Crucially, this nonreciprocal transport is strictly confined to a narrow field regime where superconductivity coexists with a field-induced spin-polarized state near a first-order metamagnetic phase boundary. The absence of the SDE away from this slender phase-intersection argues strongly against purely extrinsic vortex pinning asymmetries. Instead, our findings indicate spontaneous inversion symmetry breaking accompanied by finite-momentum Cooper pairing. We model this behavior using a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau theory, demonstrating that the intertwining of magnetic and triplet superconducting orders can stabilize an odd-parity FFLO state.

papers.abstract: We establish an experimentally accessible route to identifying Majorana surface states through their intrinsic Ising spin response, using UTe$_2$ as a concrete platform. The key is to extend the Majorana correlations into an adjacent metallic film via the superconducting proximity effect, thereby making the otherwise surface-localized response accessible to NMR measurements. Remarkably, disorder further sharpens the Majorana signature: impurity scattering suppresses the conventional $p$-wave proximity correlations while preserving the Majorana contribution, yielding a giant Ising-anisotropic enhancement of the NMR relaxation rate. This approach also offers a powerful means to distinguish among candidate pairing symmetries.

papers.abstract: Unconventional superconductors with a two-component order parameter support the existence of a rotational symmetry breaking nematic phase and a time-reversal symmetry breaking chiral phase. A recent experiment on 4Hb-TaS$_2$ surprisingly shows both twofold anisotropy in $H_{c2}$, which suggests nematic superconductivity, as well as isotropic vortices at low temperatures, which suggest chiral superconductivity. To resolve this apparent conundrum we write down the appropriate Ginzburg-Landau equations and develop a numerically efficient algorithm for finding vortex solutions, allowing us to study their shape and anisotropy over a broad parameter range. We also demonstrate analytically that, to leading order, the vortex anisotropy is independent of strain in the nematic case, but is linearly dependent on it in the chiral phase, providing a possible way to distinguish the two phases. Using all these results we show that, in the presence of strain, in a large parameter regime the system behaves nematically near the transition, leading to an anisotropy of $H_{c2}$, but is dominantly chiral away from the transition, leading to parametrically smaller vortex anisotropy, in line with the experiment.
papers.physics_advance: In a broad parameter regime, strain permits nematic behavior near the transition but predominantly chiral behavior farther below it; vortex anisotropy is strain-independent to leading order for the nematic phase and linear in strain for the chiral phase.
papers.relevance_reason: The paper develops a superconducting-order-parameter theory that addresses observed anisotropy through a concrete prediction distinguishing chiral from nematic superconductivity.

This behavior is consistent with the combination of observations reported for 4Hb-TaS₂.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic fluctuations in Luttinger liquids
papers.summary_en: The paper develops a fluctuating two-fluid hydrodynamic theory for one-dimensional quantum liquids, distinguishing exponentially slow equilibration from power-law thermalization. It applies the theory to Coulomb-coupled wires to predict signatures in density response, drag, and near-field heat transfer.

papers.abstract: We develop the theory of hydrodynamic fluctuations for one-dimensional quantum liquids. At low temperatures the relaxation of interacting electrons in a single-channel wire separates into two classes: equilibration, which changes the numbers of right and left movers through backscattering and is exponentially slow, and thermalization, which redistributes energy and momentum at a fixed number of movers at a power-law rate. This separation of time scales gives the electron liquid a two-fluid description analogous to superfluid $^4$He, with the zero mode of the Luttinger liquid as the superfluid component and the gas of thermal excitations as the normal component. Using Onsager reciprocity and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, we add Langevin fluxes to the two-fluid hydrodynamic equations, including a mutual-friction noise generated by rare backscattering events that has no counterpart in helium. We apply the theory to Coulomb-coupled quantum wires and calculate the dynamic structure factors, which contain a second-sound peak next to the plasmon doublet; the Coulomb drag resistivity, where intrawire equilibration acts as a bottleneck and turns the hydrodynamic drag into an activated temperature dependence; and the near-field heat transfer between the wires. Mode frequencies, spectral weights, linewidths, and the crossover scales of the transport coefficients are expressed through the thermodynamic properties of the liquid and a few dissipative coefficients, providing spectroscopic and transport probes of two-fluid behavior in one-dimensional quantum systems.
papers.physics_advance: The theory predicts a two-fluid hydrodynamic regime in Luttinger liquids, including a second-sound peak, an activated Coulomb-drag dependence from the equilibration bottleneck, and mutual-friction noise from rare backscattering.
papers.relevance_reason: This develops experimentally relevant hydrodynamics and transport predictions for interacting one-dimensional quantum electrons, including distinctive signatures of two-fluid behavior.

papers.abstract: In rare-earth compounds, the interplay between geometric frustration and unusual single-ion anisotropy caused by the crystal electric field often leads to exotic magnetic phases. Here, we investigate the magnetic properties of the rare-earth Shastry-Sutherland compound Er$_2$Be$_2$GeO$_7$ using bulk measurements and neutron scattering down to sub-Kelvin temperatures. A $k=(0,0,0)$ stripe-like antiferromagnetic order with locally tilted Er$^{3+}$ moments is revealed by time-of-flight neutron powder diffraction, accompanied with a $λ$-shape specific-heat anomaly at $T_N=0.84$ K. The temperature dependence of the magnetic peak intensity corresponding to the ordered moment of Er$^{3+}$ approximates to the two-dimensional Ising universality class. Thermal- and cold-neutron inelastic scattering experiments demonstrate that the strong Ising anisotropy originates from the local crystal electric field, and reveal gapped magnetic excitations with weak dispersion in the ordered state. Mean-field random-phase approximation with inequivalent nearest-neighbor couplings accounts well for the collective excitations, while classical Monte Carlo simulations yield the fractional $1/4$ and $1/2$ magnetization plateaus. Our work provides a comprehensive description of the spin correlations in Er$_2$Be$_2$GeO$_7$ with a particular focus on the classical origin of its fractional magnetization plateaus.
papers.physics_advance: Er2Be2GeO7 has stripe-like antiferromagnetic order with locally tilted moments, strong crystal-field-derived Ising anisotropy, and weakly dispersive gapped excitations; its order-parameter behavior is consistent with the two-dimensional Ising universality clas
papers.relevance_reason: Neutron scattering and bulk measurements establish distinctive low-temperature magnetic order and excitations in a frustrated rare-earth quantum magnet.
papers.summary_zh: 作者研究 Shastry–Sutherland Ising 化合物 Er2Be2GeO7 的磁有序与自旋动力学，发现其在 TN = 0.84 K 以下形成 k = (0,0,0) 条纹状反铁磁序。他们还观测到有能隙且色散较弱的激发，并通过建模解释这些激发及分数磁化平台。
papers.method_en: The work combines bulk measurements, time-of-flight neutron powder diffraction, and thermal- and cold-neutron inelastic scattering down to sub-kelvin temperatures, with mean-field random-phase-approximation modeling and classical Monte Carlo simulations.

papers.result_en: Neutron diffraction reveals k = (0,0,0) stripe-like antiferromagnetic order with locally tilted Er3+ moments, accompanied by a lambda-shaped specific-heat anomaly at TN = 0.84 K; the ordered-moment intensity approximately follows two-dimensional Ising universality. Inelastic scattering finds gapped, weakly dispersive excitations, which the authors account for using inequivalent nearest-neighbor couplings and the local crystal electric field. Classical Monte Carlo simulations yield fractional 1/4 and 1/2 magnetization plateaus.
papers.result_zh: 中子衍射揭示了 k = (0,0,0) 条纹状反铁磁序及局部倾斜的 Er3+ 磁矩，并观测到 TN = 0.84 K 处的 λ 形比热异常；有序磁矩强度随温度的变化近似符合二维 Ising 普适类。非弹性散射发现有能隙且色散较弱的激发，作者以不等价最近邻耦合和局部晶体电场加以描述。经典蒙特卡洛模拟得到 1/4 和 1/2 分数磁化平台。
papers.future_en: The authors frame the work as a comprehensive account of spin correlations in Er2Be2GeO7 and emphasize clarifying the classical origin of its fractional magnetization plateaus.
papers.future_zh: 作者将该工作定位为对 Er2Be2GeO7 自旋关联的系统描述，并着重阐明其分数磁化平台的经典起源。
papers.tier_reason_en: The abstract presents a substantial, multi-technique characterization and modeling of magnetic order and excitations in a specific frustrated Ising compound, a strong fit for PRB-level condensed-matter research but not evidence of broader conceptual impact at a higher tier.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 摘要展示了对一种特定受挫 Ising 化合物的磁有序与激发所进行的多手段系统表征和建模，适合 PRB 水平的凝聚态研究；摘要所示的概念影响范围尚不足以支持更高层级。
